big_case.notes: Interim stay, not a merits judgment, but the per curiam announces a categorical rule ('There is no such thing as a "constitutional" major-questions claim') that reaches every jurisdiction-stripping statute preserving only constitutional claims, and it unblocks border-barrier construction across the Big Bend Sector under IIRIRA s.102 waivers. High practical and doctrinal salience for an application; below a merits landmark.

leakage.notes: Forward cell; its 12 logged calls (shell/file-read, dated 2026-10-29) read the provisioned record, statpack, and two corpus queries returning unrelated OT2026 applications. No CourtListener or web retrieval; no data/qp-topics access; disposition did not yet exist.

central_claims.basis: Nov 9: referred and granted by unsigned per curiam (~1,100 words), eleven days after the response.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant the stay of the W.D. Tex. injunction, by short unsigned order after referral to the full Court, within about one to two weeks of the Oct 29 response.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam: 'There is no such thing as a "constitutional" major-questions claim'; Dalton cited for statutory-authority claims not being constitutional.
central_claims.claim: If the Court addresses the merits, the ground is the jurisdictional bar: a major-questions argument is a claim of statutory authority, not a constitutional claim under s.102(c)(2)(A), with Dalton directly against respondents.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam does not reach the s.102(a) high-illegal-entry question.
central_claims.claim: The Court will likely not decide whether Big Bend is an 'area of high illegal entry'.

central_claims.basis: Only the stay is granted; no summary reversal.
central_claims.claim: The summary-reversal request will be left or denied while the stay is granted.

central_claims.basis: JUSTICE JACKSON would deny the application; no written dissent (the written-dissent part was hedged, not committed).
central_claims.claim: If granted, at least one of Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson will note a dissent; a written dissent is plausible from Sotomayor or Jackson.
